title: The Boston Globe's Western Mass lesbian bar story pulled in "several thousand" new subscribers in about 72 hours
tldr: A single deeply-reported, neutrally-written magazine feature drove several thousand subscriptions in days, proving human, nuanced storytelling still converts hard. A concrete case study in what quality journalism can do for a paywall business.
angle: What made this one story a subscription magnet — and how brands can engineer 'quiet' storytelling that converts.

title: News consumers are wary of most AI use in local news, a Chicago-based report finds
tldr: New Medill survey shows readers deeply distrust AI in news-gathering, a warning for any publisher tempted to automate. Direct evidence on how audiences actually feel about AI-made content.
why_fresh: new survey data on AI trust
angle: The trust tax of AI content: why disclosing automation may cost you more audience than it saves.

angle: From founder face to owned entertainment: the maturity curve of brand-as-publisher.

tldr: Marketers admit AI is dragging creative standards toward 'good enough,' sacrificing craft for speed. A timely tension between efficiency and quality worth interrogating.
angle: Why 'good enough — go' is a reputation time-bomb, and how human craft becomes a differentiator.

angle: Life after the link: how content strategy must adapt when AI answers replace clicks.

angle: What HubSpot's 140M lost visits teach every content team about diversifying beyond Google.
